vignette: Tano is a 24-year-old male of Oceania ethnicity, currently working as a pharmacist at a bustling hospital in the city. He remains single and has always found solace in his work, which he considers both fulfilling and demanding. Tano’s life took an unexpected turn when his younger sister, Lani, was involved in a severe car accident last year. The accident occurred late one evening when Lani was returning from her college campus. The rain had made the roads slippery, and another driver lost control of their vehicle, slamming into Lani's car at high speed. Tano received the call just as he was finishing his shift at the hospital; the urgency in his mother’s voice immediately set off alarms. Upon arriving at the hospital, Tano was greeted by a chaotic scene—emergency personnel rushing about with critical equipment and distressed family members waiting anxiously for updates. He felt an overwhelming sense of dread and helplessness as he waited for news on Lani's condition. The initial diagnosis revealed multiple fractures and internal injuries; she was in critical but stable condition. Since the accident, Tano has been preoccupied by intrusive thoughts and images of that night—flashes of the car crumpled against a pole, the sound of sirens echoing through the rain-soaked streets, and his sister’s pale face. These memories often intrude during quiet moments or when he is alone, causing him to feel intense fear and anxiety. Tano tries to cope by immersing himself in work, throwing himself into his role as a pharmacist with renewed vigor. However, this dedication comes at a cost; he has become increasingly isolated from friends and family. He often finds himself replaying the events of the accident and worrying about what might have happened differently. This constant rumination leaves him feeling exhausted and drained. At night, Tano struggles to sleep due to nightmares that vividly recreate the scene of Lani's accident. In these dreams, he is unable to save her or alleviate her pain, leaving him with a deep sense of guilt and powerlessness. Upon waking, his heart races and beads of sweat cover his forehead as he grapples with the images that haunt him. During his shifts at the hospital, Tano often finds himself distracted by intrusive thoughts about Lani’s accident. The sounds of emergency vehicles outside the pharmacy or patients arriving with traumatic injuries trigger a flood of anxiety. He becomes hypervigilant and on edge, constantly scanning for signs of distress among patients and colleagues. His attention to detail has become so intense that he sometimes forgets basic tasks or makes minor mistakes. Lani’s recovery has been slow and challenging. She underwent several surgeries and months of rehabilitation. Tano visits her frequently but the experience is bittersweet—seeing his sister in pain and struggling to regain strength evokes deep sadness and frustration within him. He often withdraws emotionally during these visits, feeling a mix of helplessness and guilt for not being able to prevent the accident. Despite his efforts to stay engaged with work, Tano finds it increasingly difficult to connect with others on a personal level. His close friends notice that he has become distant and irritable, though they do not fully understand why. He avoids social gatherings and outings, preferring instead to spend time alone or working late at the hospital. Tano’s experience of PTSD is deeply intertwined with his love for Lani and the profound sense of loss and vulnerability triggered by her accident. His life has been marked by a constant struggle between his dedication to work and the overwhelming emotional burden he carries. Tano remains committed to supporting Lani but finds himself grappling with the lingering effects of trauma, which continue to shape his daily experiences and interactions.
